newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Flexibility in euro goals inappropriateB - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: Flexibility in euro goals inappropriateB - Tietmeyer.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer told a Lisbon newspaper that a flexible interpretation of convergence criteria for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) was inappropriate and countries must show sustained discipline.

"I think it would not be appropriate to take a flexible approach to the criteria as sustainability is what matters," Tietmeyer told the Portuguese-language Publico newspaper in an interview published on Wednesday.
He visited Lisbon on Monday and Tuesday to attend 150th anniversary celebrations of the Bank of Portugal.
"The essential point is the sustainability of efforts to achieve convergence," Tietmeyer said.

"This (sustainability) is the main criterion for me because there is a danger of jeopardising the necessary credibility for the start of EMU, which must produce a stable and strong currency," he added.
Tietmeyer said he would be pleased if the single currency, the euro, were as strong as the German mark.

Asked if interest rates linked to the euro would be higher or lower than the present level of German rates, he said: "I hope they would be lower, but this would depend on whether the euro turns out to be a strong currency or not."
He added: "If the euro were a weak currency, then interest rates would be higher."
Tietmeyer declined to comment on individual countries' efforts to meet the economic targets set to join the euro.
"No one can predict with accuracy the results (of countries' efforts to join the euro)," he said.
"We will have to wait until the beginning of 1998 to see what will be the results," he added.
Under the 1992 Maastricht Treaty, states wanting to take part in currency union must fulfil five criteria during 1997 indicating robust economic health.

These are a debt-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio of less than 60 percent, a budget deficit lower than three percent of GDP, low inflation, low long-term interest rates and exemplary membership of Europe's existing currency grid for two years.
